# IdeaVim fixtures this host does not match yet.
#
# Generated by VimFixtureReplayTest, which writes the current list to
# build/fixture-failures.txt with the difference for each one, and a header saying how many were
# harvested and why the rest were not. To update this file, read that one and copy the names across
# - never edit a name by hand to make the build pass.
#
# 1030 of the 1049 harvested fixtures pass. These nineteen are grouped by what is actually wrong,
# which is seven things.
#
# The corpus grew by 24 when the harness stopped refusing fixtures with more than one caret, and
# twelve of those twenty-four fail. That is the yield of removing a refusal, and it is why refusing
# is only ever a temporary answer: multiple cursors are the feature VS Code is best known for, and
# every one of these is IdeaVim saying what a multi-caret command should do.
#
# Four entries left this list without anything being fixed, which is the other thing to remember
# about it: the harness was typing setup commands through `parseKeys`, so `:nmap <Tab> ihello<Esc>`
# pressed Escape on the command line instead of writing five characters into it. Four fixtures had
# been recorded here as bugs in this host that were bugs in the harness reading them.

# --- A caret the block rebuild reassigned, still held by the motion that caused it.
#
# This is one bug and it accounts for eight of the entries below. The shape is unmistakable in the
# difference: `caret expected [18, 47, 86, 127], actual [47, 86, 127, 127]` - the first caret is
# missing, the last is there twice, and everything in between has slid along by one.
#
# What happens is that a vertical motion in blockwise Visual asks the *host* to lay the block out
# again, and the engine's `vimSetSystemBlockSelectionSilently` is documented to invalidate the caret
# the motion is running on: "WARNING! This can invalidate the primary caret". IntelliJ's selection
# model really does replace its caret objects there, so the motion's own final move lands on a caret
# that has been thrown away. This host reuses the caret instead - `vimSelectionStart` is stored on
# the instance, so the anchor has to survive - and it becomes the block's *first* line, since that
# is the line it is on when the block is rebuilt. The motion then moves it to the destination on the
# *last* line, and the first line's caret is dragged to the bottom of the block.
#
# Traced by logging the caret moves for `<C-V>jl`:
#     setBlock rebuilt=[(caret-1, 16, (15, 16)), (caret-2, 47, (46, 47))]
#     caret-1 moveToVisualPosition(line=2, column=2) 16 -> 15
#     caret-2 moveToVisualPosition(line=3, column=2) 47 -> 46
#     caret-1 moveToInlayAwareOffset(46) from 15      <- the motion, on the wrong caret
#
# So the fix is about what a host owes a caret the engine has just re-purposed, and it is a separate
# piece of work from reading these fixtures at all.
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/select/SelectToggleVisualModeHandlerTest.kt:test switch to select mode blockwise left motion
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/visual/VisualToggleCharacterModeActionTest.kt:test enter visual with count after block visual operation
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/visual/VisualToggleCharacterModeActionTest.kt:test enter visual with count after block visual operation multiple time
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/visual/VisualToggleCharacterModeActionTest.kt:test enter visual with count after visual operation multicaret
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/visual/VisualToggleCharacterModeActionTest.kt:test enter visual with double count after block visual operation
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/action/motion/visual/VisualToggleCharacterModeActionTest.kt:test enter visual with ten count after block visual operation
src/test/java/org/jetbrains/plugins/ideavim/group/SearchGroupTest.kt:test cancelling search restores Visual (blockwise)

# [19, 42, 104]` on `Ve<C-G>`, and `expected [12], actual [12, 12]` on a block Select reaching an
# empty line. The engine narrows a multi-caret selection back to fewer carets and this host keeps
# the ones it was told to drop - close kin to the entry above, and possibly the same fix.

# --- Reindenting, which is a VS Code command and therefore asynchronous.

# --- An IntelliJ action replayed by `.`, which this host has no equivalent of.
